title: Chapter 55 — Showroom Events
intro: Using your showroom as a trade development platform — event formats, invitations, and pipeline conversion.

sections.title: Event Formats That Work
sections.content:
The after-hours designer evening: food, drinks, and a focused product demo. Keep it to 90 minutes. Feature one or two brands. Let designers touch, open, and experience the products without retail customers around. This is their private preview.

The cooking demo: invite a local chef to cook on your pro-style ranges. Invite builders, designers, and their clients. Nothing sells a Wolf range like watching a chef use one while you eat what they cook.

The CEU session: partner with a manufacturer to offer continuing education credits. Designers need CEUs to maintain their certifications. You provide the education. They remember who provided it.

The builder spec night: invite builders for a 60-minute session on new products, rebate programs, and package pricing for the upcoming building season. Practical, not flashy.

sections.title: The Invitation Strategy
sections.content:
Curate the guest list from your CRM. Invite active accounts to maintain the relationship. Invite prospects to create the relationship. Invite one or two prominent designers or builders whose attendance signals credibility to others.

Personal invitations convert 3-5 times higher than mass emails. Call or text each invitee directly: 'We are hosting a private event for designers on Thursday — I think you would find it valuable. Can I save you a spot?'

sections.title: Converting After the Event
sections.content:
Follow up with every attendee within 48 hours. 'Great seeing you Thursday night. You mentioned you have a project coming up with a luxury kitchen — can I put together a spec package for you?'

The event warms the relationship. The follow-up converts it. Skip the follow-up and the event was a party, not a business development activity.
